newsitem.title: SOMALIA: 15 killed in fighting in northern Mogadishu.
newsitem.headline: 15 killed in fighting in northern Mogadishu.

text.p: At least 14 people were killed in heavy fighting on Wednesday between gunmen loyal to a north Mogadishu faction leader and an Islamic leader, hospital sources and witnesses said.
They said at least 32 people were wounded in the fighting between gunmen using "technical" four-wheel-drive battlewagons, anti-tank rockets, mortar bombs, heavy machineguns and rifles.

A spokesman for Islamic leader Sheikh Ali Dhere described it as a war between Islamic militiamen and gunmen who opposed the pacification of north Mogadishu, controlled by powerful faction leader Ali Mahdi Mohamed's forces and Islamic gunmen.
The fighting blocked the main business junctions of north Mogadishu and roads leading to the main Islamic court were cut.
The dead included three civilians killed by a mortar bomb that hit their house and two children hit by a rocket-propelled grenade. More than 50 families fled their homes for safer areas.
Shooting eased in the afternoon but both sides remained at their positions and it resumed in the afternoon. It was the worst bloodshed between Islamic court supporters and Ali Mahdis gunmen.
Fighting spread in the afternoon from Shibbis district, where Dhere has his headquarters, to Abdulziz and Karan areas.
The spokesman for Dhere said 40 prisoners were released by the Islamic courts on Wednesday for their own safety as the Islamic militiamen who guard the prison were engaged in battle.
A spokesman for Ali Mahdi said the fighting was between Dhere's supporters and "independent" gunmen who attacked the Islamic leader's convoy on Wednesday, killing one civilian and wounding four.
Ali Mahdi's supporters were widely suspected to have been behind the ambush.
Relations have been tense since October when Ali Mahdi, a self-styled president, dismissed Dhere as chairman of north Mogadishu's supreme Islamic court, which was established two years ago.

Somalia has had no central government since the overthrow of late dictator Mohamed Siad Barre in 1991 but the establishment of the Islamic courts with popular support after years of lawlessness brought a degree of security to north Mogadishu.
